answer: Curing a proof takes 13 days, and a farm holding 120 proofs cannot cure them side by side. Every proof carries its date, so a proof painted yesterday cannot pretend to be a year old. Stories stop at the door; only each iron is a tin count weighed beside the maker's mark walks through, and Tin trimmer iron warrant soldered into the plating vat is the one asking for it. Walk the trail by hand: it is short enough to walk and long enough to trip a farm. When the voyage and the pigment tell one story and the opal tells another, believe the opal: nurseries are harder to forge than names.
